parsed.explanation: The division itself is strongly protective: GENDA public-accommodations coverage since 2019, a 2024 constitutional amendment, a gender-identity hate-crimes statute with recent reform, a shield law for visiting patients, mandated gender-neutral bathrooms, repeal of the loitering provision used against trans people, self-affirmed marker change and an X marker on state documents, and courts/police that have acted. That is documented protective machinery actually operating, well above the national line. But the national layer governs the chokepoints every visitor must pass: sex-marker restrictions, discontinued X passports, screening guidance inviting refusal and possible lifetime fraud findings where documents are doubted, reported detentions of travellers over visa issues, allied governments issuing trans-specific advisories, facility exclusion in federally controlled buildings, and documented severe abuse of trans people in immigration custody. The state cannot override these. Not tier-3 hostility, but a real unremedied visitor-facing exposure at the border and in federal custody, so below the 0.65 tier.
